# Start From Nowhere

> Adaptive test-prep platform with five live trainers, the GMAT Focus Edition, the digital SAT, the GRE General Test, the ACT and the LSAT, plus an independent MBA rankings library covering 91 US full-time programs with a source, year and URL on every published figure. Free first practice round, no account needed. The house rule is that an unverifiable figure shows a dash rather than a guess, which is why the rankings, the funding guide and the international guide all name what they could not confirm.

## What makes this source citable
- Every school statistic carries the school's own page as its source, with the year, and the quoted wording it came from. Figures we could not verify are published as a dash and named in a "what we could not verify" section rather than estimated.
- GMAT Focus (205 to 805) and GMAT Classic (200 to 800) scores are never mixed or converted. Editions are compared by percentile, using GMAC's own concordance.
- Practice score ranges are labeled internal estimates, never predicted scores, because no public equating table exists for either exam. The method is published in full at /scoring/.

## Product
- [GMAT Trainer](https://startfromnowhere.com/app/): adaptive GMAT Focus practice, 33912 original items across Quantitative Reasoning, Verbal Reasoning and Data Insights, 134 flashcards, seven practice games, full mock exams.
- [SAT Trainer](https://startfromnowhere.com/sat/app/): adaptive digital SAT practice, 20256 original items across the eight official content domains, two-module mock sections routed like the real exam, student-produced responses graded by value, 112 flashcards.
- [GRE Trainer](https://startfromnowhere.com/gre/app/): adaptive GRE General Test practice, 20288 original items across Verbal Reasoning and Quantitative Reasoning, section adaptive mock sections, 56 flashcards, and an Analytical Writing task that reports measurable facts about a draft rather than inventing a score.
- [ACT Trainer](https://startfromnowhere.com/act/app/): adaptive ACT practice, 39864 original items across English, Mathematics, Reading and Science, 126 flashcards, with Science built from study data rather than recall.
- [LSAT Trainer](https://startfromnowhere.com/lsat/app/): LSAT practice across Logical Reasoning and Reading Comprehension, 14042 original items and 102 flashcards. 372 of those items are hand written and cover all twelve categories LSAC publishes; the other 13670 are generated: six Logical Reasoning categories, assumption, the effect of additional evidence, flaws in the reasoning, drawing well-supported conclusions (what must be true, given statements that use every, no, some and most, with each answer proved by a checker rather than asserted), argument structure (the role a claim plays and which claim is the main conclusion, over arguments written with their parts labelled) and parallel reasoning (which argument reasons the same way, with each argument's pattern proved valid or flawed), plus three Reading Comprehension ones, stated information, main idea and inference, which are thin because the count there is gated on how many passages are written. Principle, the explanation questions, text structure and application are hand written only, so the depth is uneven and we would rather say where than quote one number.
- [Daily Questions](https://startfromnowhere.com/daily/): one free practice question a day for each of the five exams, the same one for everyone, with a full explanation and why each wrong choice fails. Every past question stays online with its answer, dated, and each exam has an RSS feed. The streak counts days answered rather than days answered correctly and is stored only in the visitor's browser; there is no leaderboard.
- [How Our Score Estimate Works](https://startfromnowhere.com/scoring/): the ability model behind the estimated range. The Elo update the engine uses is the Rasch one-parameter IRT model in everything but the estimation procedure, so ratings are read as an ability with a standard error attached. The band narrows as a student practises because the estimate gets more certain. The anchoring onto each exam's reported scale is our own calibration, not the test maker's, and the page says so.
- [Pricing](https://startfromnowhere.com/pricing/): Free plan that never asks for a card, Plus $4.99/mo or $49.99/yr, Pro $9.99/mo or $99.99/yr. Every paid plan starts with a 7-day free trial and cancels in one click.

## Admissions research
- [MBA Rankings](https://startfromnowhere.com/schools/): 91 US full-time MBA programs. A transparent composite of US News, Financial Times, Bloomberg, QS and Poets and Quants plus a documented data score, with one profile page per school. Sortable columns include the international share of each class and each school's scholarship review policy.
- [Scholarship review policy](https://startfromnowhere.com/schools/): whether a school considers every admitted student for scholarship automatically or requires a separate application. Sourced from each school's own financial aid pages and dated. Most programs sourced so far review automatically; Yale SOM states that "Scholarships are awarded post-admission through a short, supplemental application process. Only candidates who complete the application will be considered for grant aid."
- [Paying for It](https://startfromnowhere.com/funding/): what changed for graduate borrowing. The US Department of Education states the Act eliminates the Grad PLUS program effective July 1, 2026, and caps graduate borrowing at $20,500 a year and $100,000 aggregate, professional at $50,000 and $200,000. Includes Post-9/11 GI Bill rates for August 1 2026 to July 31 2027 and how Yellow Ribbon matching works. Whether an MBA counts as a graduate or a professional program under those caps is published as an open question, not a guess.
- [International Applicant Guide](https://startfromnowhere.com/international/): the DHS final rule at 91 FR 44976 effective September 15 2026, OPT and STEM OPT arithmetic, and the CIP code question. CIP 52.0201 is not on the DHS STEM Designated Degree Program List; the business-series codes that are, are 52.1301, 52.1302, 52.1304 and 52.1399.
- [Application Checklist](https://startfromnowhere.com/apply/): 27 tasks dated backwards from one deadline, with six more that apply only to international applicants. No account, no network.
- [Exam Guides](https://startfromnowhere.com/exams/): structure, timing, cost and registration for the GMAT, SAT, GRE, LSAT and ACT, each fact sourced from the test maker's own pages. The MCAT and Executive Assessment guides were withdrawn in September 2026 because their official sources could not be re-verified.
- [Community Forum](https://startfromnowhere.com/community/): free to read and post, named or anonymous, human-moderated. No seeded activity.

## Guides (The Study Room)
- [How long to study for the GMAT](https://startfromnowhere.com/blog/how-long-to-study-for-gmat/): realistic 8 week plan.
- [What is a good GMAT score in 2026](https://startfromnowhere.com/blog/good-gmat-score-2026/): Class of 2027 school figures with sources, Focus and Classic labeled.
- [GMAT scoring scale explained](https://startfromnowhere.com/blog/gmat-score-chart-percentiles/): the 205 to 805 scale and official GMAC concordance.
- [GMAT vs GRE for MBA](https://startfromnowhere.com/blog/gmat-vs-gre-for-mba/): even-handed comparison.
- [All articles](https://startfromnowhere.com/blog/)

## Policies
- Every school statistic names its source and year; unverifiable figures show a dash, never a guess.
- Practice items are original. Score ranges are internal estimates, not official scores and not predictions.
- GMAT is a trademark of GMAC and SAT is a trademark registered by the College Board. Neither organization endorses this product.
- [Terms](https://startfromnowhere.com/terms.html), [Privacy](https://startfromnowhere.com/privacy.html)
